title: "The exercise"
subtitle: "Analyst no. 6"
---

This page sets out the exercise of the short session, task by task, with the tool in which each task is done. The [background page](../../cases/europeanisation/index.qmd) presents the original study, the robustness study of SCORE (Multi100; Aczel et al. 2026) and the five reanalyses in full, and it is the place to start if you have not read it. Every task of the session is done in its deck, whose slides run R inside your browser with the data already in place, and the [browser lab](../../cases/europeanisation/lab.qmd), a page of this site that holds the same tasks, is the fallback if the deck will not load.

## The tasks {#the-tasks}

The session takes three of the five tasks of the exercise at the keyboard, all three in the deck, and keeps the estimand statement of Task 2 as an answer that you write in the chat. The causal graph of Task 2 and the preregistration of Task 5 are left to the [one-day workshop](../europeanisation-one-day/index.qmd) and the [self-study route](../self-study/index.qmd). The page of each half lists its steps, and each step at the keyboard has a button that opens the deck at the slide of the task, beside one that opens the browser lab at the same task, as the fallback.

### Task 1 – Get yourself running {#task-1-get-yourself-running}

The only aim is to reach the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you. Open the deck, wait until the cell on its second slide shows a "Run Code" button, run it, and check that it reports 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years; Task 1 of the [browser lab](../../cases/europeanisation/lab.qmd#task-1-setup) holds the same check.

### The estimand statement {#the-estimand-statement}

The five analysts answered five questions. On the slides of the first half, write the estimand of the claim in one sentence, hold it, and send it with the rest of the class when the facilitator says go.

### Task 3 – Reproduce a recorded result {#task-3-reproduce-a-recorded-result}

Choose one of the three analysts whose results rest on aggregate data, C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL, and refit the analysis until the value on record comes back to the third decimal. Each of the three has a slide of its own in the deck, whose cells you run in order, and each cell with gaps to fill has a hint and a full solution under it; the page of the [first half](half-1.qmd#task-3-the-reproduction) gives the data, the model and the value on record for each. Type the analyst and the value into the chat, for example `KQXUE t = -7.169`, hold it, and send it when the facilitator says go. In the deck the two packages of the model of 018OL load when the deck is opened, while in the [browser lab](../../cases/europeanisation/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction) the second cell of 018OL downloads them, about 32 MB.

### Task 4 – Work the menu {#task-4-work-the-menu}

This task is **exploratory**. On the three slides of the hands-on in the second half, call `try_spec()` three or four times, changing one argument at a time, and print the tries side by side with `my_experiments()`. Every argument of `try_spec()` defaults to the reproduced specification, the model of C6HJR on which the [specification menu](../../cases/europeanisation/menu.qmd) and the curve are built, and an option that is off the curve stops with the reason why and the page of the course that teaches it. Then submit the one that you would defend with `submit_exploration()`, and your dot is drawn on the live [class chart](../../cases/europeanisation/class-results.qmd) as an exploratory result.

In the cell of the placement slide, rerun the specification that you submitted with `try_spec()`, read off your placement among the 864 specifications of the curve, hold it, and send it when the facilitator says go. Without a submission of your own, use the placement of the reproduced specification, 67%. The [browser lab](../../cases/europeanisation/lab.qmd#task-4-explore) holds the same cells.
